snip.t: The underlying etiology is a likely autoimmune reaction to the parasitic worm Onchocerca volvulus.
Extrinsic compression: Obstruction caused by external pressure on the bowel, such as from adhesions (post-surgical), hernias (incarcerated bowel), volvulus (twisting of the bowel), or masses.
Gastric volvulus: Occasionally, a massive intrathoracic hiatus hernia may twist upon itself, leading to a gastric\nvolvulus.

qs.q: A patient infected with Onchocerca volvulus receives an antihelminthic agent and subsequently develops a Mazzotti reaction characterized by fever and rash due to dying microfilariae. Which drug was most likely administered?
o: Albendazole utilized for systemic tissue parasite
Praziquantel given for blood fluke infestation
qs.e: Ivermectin treats onchocerciasis and can trigger the Mazzotti reaction when the immune system responds to dying microfilariae. Mebendazole has minimal systemic absorption and rarely causes severe systemic inflammatory reactions.

qs.q: A health worker recommends straightening of rivers as a physical control measure against the vector transmitting Onchocerca volvulus. Which vector is targeted?
qs.e: Simulium neavei transmits Onchocerca volvulus, and river straightening serves as a physical control. Culex species transmit Wuchereria bancrofti.

qs.q: Onchocerca volvulus is mainly transmitted by
o: Limited to a single tissue compartment
qs.e: Simulium species (blackflies) are the exclusive vectors of Onchocerca volvulus, causing onchocerciasis (river blindness). These flies breed in fast-flowing, well-oxygenated water bodies, explaining why the disease is associated with river systems in endemic areas.

qs.q: The black fly (Simulium species) transmits the parasitic nematode Onchocerca volvulus, which causes river blindness (onchocerciasis).
qs.e: Black flies, belonging to the genus Simulium, are the vectors for the parasite Onchocerca volvulus, the causative agent of onchocerciasis, commonly known as river blindness. This disease is prevalent in parts of Africa and Latin America.
